exercises.name: Mmmm ladder
exercises.details: Hum the notes and listen for the resonance when you’re on pitch. If you’re not on pitch, try to tell if you’re too high/ low yourself, while only looking at the screen periodically.

exercises.name: Mom Moh
exercises.details: Widen your nasal cavities and envision the sound projecting into the nose and forehead. (Todo: change words)

exercises.name: Brrrr
exercises.details: Keep your lips loose and let them flutter on steady air, like a motorboat. Focus on keeping everything relaxed.

exercises.name: Moo
exercises.details: Round your lips into a small "Oo" and restart every note with a gentle "M". Don't push for volume.

exercises.name: Ng
exercises.details: Hum on "ng" with your lips apart and your jaw loose. You should feel a buzz behind your nose.

exercises.name: Mee May Mah Moh Moo
exercises.details: Keep the "M" buzzing in your lips and change only the vowel. Your jaw should stay loose and still.

exercises.name: Vee
exercises.details: Rest your top teeth lightly on your lower lip and keep the air buzzing. The steady "V" helps you keep your airflow even.

exercises.name: Mmm Mah
exercises.details: Hum the way up with your lips closed, then open into "Mah" at the top. Keep the same buzzing resonance as your mouth opens.

exercises.name: Hoo
exercises.details: Start with a soft, breathy "H" and let the "Oo" float down. Keep it light, like a gentle owl call.

exercises.name: Nyah
exercises.details: Make a bright, bratty "Nyah", like a teasing child. You should feel the sound buzzing in your nose and cheekbones.

exercises.name: Ming
exercises.details: Sing a short, bright "Ming" on every note and let the "ng" ring. Keep your throat open and your tongue relaxed.

exercises.name: Nee Nay Nah
exercises.details: Keep the sound forward in your face as the vowel opens from "Nee" to "Nah". Don't let the "Nah" fall back into your throat.

exercises.name: Gah
exercises.details: Keep the back of your tongue loose on each "G" and let your jaw drop on the "Ah". The "G" helps your vocal folds close cleanly.

exercises.name: Wee Woo
exercises.details: Make "Wee" bright and "Woo" round and dark. Keep the change between them smooth, like a gentle siren.

exercises.name: Nuh
exercises.details: Use a dopey, speech-like "Nuh" to keep your larynx from rising. Stay relaxed and don't push for volume.

exercises.name: Three-Note Scale
exercises.details: Hear each note in your head before you sing it and match it exactly. Keep your tone even from bottom to top.

exercises.name: Chromatic Steps
exercises.details: Every step is a semitone, the smallest step in the scale. Keep the steps small and even without sliding between notes.

exercises.name: Five-Note Scale
exercises.details: Keep every step even and your tone the same from the bottom note to the top.

exercises.name: Minor Five-Note Scale
exercises.details: The third note sits lower than in the major scale. Listen closely and tune it carefully on the way up and down.

exercises.name: Descending Five-Note Scale
exercises.details: Start the top note lightly and keep that lightness as you go down. Don't let your voice get heavier on the low notes.

exercises.name: Broken Thirds
exercises.details: Think of the scale underneath the skips, so every note lands in tune.

exercises.name: Major Triad
exercises.details: Aim for the centre of each note instead of sliding into it. Hear the next note in your head before you sing it.

exercises.name: Minor Triad
exercises.details: The minor third is a little narrower than the major one. Hear it in your head before you sing it.

exercises.name: Major Scale Up and Down
exercises.details: Take a full breath before each repetition and pace your air across the whole scale.

exercises.name: Harmonic Minor Scale
exercises.details: Listen for the wide step between the sixth and seventh notes, which gives this scale its distinctive sound.

exercises.name: Pentatonic Scale
exercises.details: This five-note scale has no semitones and is heard in folk and pop music around the world. Keep the skips in tune.

exercises.name: Ninth Scale
exercises.details: Stay light as you pass the octave and don't reach up for the top note.

exercises.name: Ta Ka
exercises.details: Alternate the tip and the back of your tongue, like double tonguing on a flute. Keep the notes crisp and the air steady.

exercises.name: Tongue Trill
exercises.details: Roll your tongue on a steady stream of air, like a purring cat. If you can't roll your R yet, use a lip trill instead.

exercises.name: Ti Ki Ta
exercises.details: Tip, back, tip: keep the three syllables even and crisp, and let the air flow through them.

exercises.name: La Le Li Lo Lu
exercises.details: Flick the tip of your tongue for each "L" and keep your jaw still. Only your tongue should move.

exercises.name: Ning Nong
exercises.details: Switch between the bright "Ning" and the darker "Nong" while keeping the "ng" buzzing in the same place.

exercises.name: Dee Dah
exercises.details: Keep your tongue light and quick and make the two vowels clearly different.

exercises.name: Hup
exercises.details: Push each "Hup" out with a small kick from your belly, like a short laugh. Your throat should stay relaxed.

exercises.name: Kah Gah
exercises.details: Use light, quick "K" and "G" sounds from the back of your tongue. Keep the vowel open behind them.

exercises.name: Ta Da La Na
exercises.details: Four tongue shapes in a row. Keep them quick and light and don't let your jaw join in.

exercises.name: Pa Ba
exercises.details: Keep your lips springy and your throat relaxed. Let the air carry you through the consonants without stopping.

exercises.name: Pa Ta Ka
exercises.details: Keep "Pa Ta Ka" crisp and quick, like a patter song. Let the air keep flowing so the notes don't get choppy.

exercises.name: Buh Duh Guh
exercises.details: Voiced consonants from the lips, the tip and the back of the tongue. Keep your voice going through each consonant so the notes stay connected.

exercises.name: da da da speed up
exercises.details: Focus on keeping the pitch unchanging, with quick transitions from note to note.

exercises.name: Accelerating Trill
exercises.details: Each repetition is a little faster. Keep the two notes even and relaxed as the tempo rises.

exercises.name: Half-Step Trill
exercises.details: The two notes are only a semitone apart. Keep them clearly separate without letting them blur together.

exercises.name: Five-Note Run
exercises.details: Maintain a steady airflow and consistent mouth placement.

exercises.name: Rolling Triplets
exercises.details: Feel the notes in groups of three, with a slight lean on the first note of each group.

exercises.name: Staccato Scale
exercises.details: Make every "Ha" short and crisp, with a small pulse from your belly. Keep your throat relaxed between the notes.

exercises.name: Scale Sequence
exercises.details: The same four-note figure moves up one step at a time. Keep each group even and in tune.

exercises.name: Turns
exercises.details: Sing the little turns around each main note cleanly and lightly, without smudging them.

exercises.name: Pentatonic Riff
exercises.details: A short riff in the style of pop and soul singing. Keep it light and loose and let each note speak clearly.

exercises.name: Octave Run
exercises.details: Sing each repetition on a different vowel. Maintain a steady airflow and consistent mouth placement.

exercises.name: Nine-Note Run
exercises.details: Sing the whole run on one breath and keep the notes even. Take a quick, low breath between repetitions.

exercises.name: Descending Octave Run
exercises.details: Start the top note light and let the run fall evenly, without rushing at the bottom.

exercises.name: Arpeggio Run
exercises.details: Keep every note of the arpeggio clear and connected. Aim for the centre of each note instead of sliding.

exercises.name: Fifth Leap Nay
exercises.details: Leap to the top note without reaching or pushing, then let the scale carry you back down.

exercises.name: Sixth Leap Ee
exercises.details: Keep the "Ee" narrow and bright on the leap and don't let your jaw drop to reach the top.

exercises.name: Octave Leap and Scale
exercises.details: Jump straight to the top note without scooping, then keep your voice light as the scale comes down.

exercises.name: Octave Siren Oo
exercises.details: Glide between the notes like a siren, without a break in the sound. Let your voice get lighter as it rises.

exercises.name: Octave Arpeggio Yah
exercises.details: Keep your mouth shape the same all the way up and let the top note be lighter, not louder.

exercises.name: Scale Up, Arpeggio Down
exercises.details: Climb the scale step by step and come back down in bigger skips. Keep the top note as easy as the bottom one.

exercises.name: Octave Lip Trill
exercises.details: Let your lips flutter on steady air through the whole octave. If the trill stops, loosen your lips and use a little more air.

exercises.name: Minor Arpeggio Nah
exercises.details: Keep the "Nah" bright and forward all the way up, so the top note doesn't feel like a reach.

exercises.name: Top-Down Arpeggio
exercises.details: Start on the top note in a light voice and carry that lightness down to the bottom and back up again.

exercises.name: Tenth Arpeggio
exercises.details: Keep your breath flowing through the top of the arpeggio and don't grab the high note.

exercises.name: Octave Jumps Ha
exercises.details: Use short, bouncy "Ha" sounds powered by your belly, not your throat. Stay relaxed on the jumps.

exercises.name: Octave and a Half Arpeggio
exercises.details: Let the top notes thin out and get lighter. If you feel strain, stop and rest before trying again.
